# MREC, SMA-star and iterative threshold search

Three source-scoped memory-bounded search procedures: MREC, simplified memory-bounded A-star search and iterative threshold search. Exact accepted definitions,12 claims24 limitations and three primary artifacts are preserved. Twenty-two bibliography objects retain28 occurrences, six search-only leads and unresolved MA*/IE source questions, with current explicit responsibility.

Memory-search source responsibility: Twenty-two exact bibliography objects retain28 source occurrences, six search-only leads, and unresolved MA*/IE original-source/identity questions. Current responsibility is explicit; no source-question count is a new-concept count or family exhaustion.

  "entries": [
    {
      "path": "data/curated/MREC.yaml",
      "disposition": "added",
      "id": "AIMech:MREC",
      "name": "MREC",
      "aliases": [],
      "definition": "A recursive heuristic search algorithm that retains an explicit search graph within available additional memory, explores unstored successors virtually when that storage is unavailable, and backs up remaining-cost estimates between bounded recursive passes.",
      "identity_notes": "MREC denotes Sen and Bagchi's 1989 recursive best-first memory-controlled procedure, with an explicitly stored graph and virtual unstored successors, backed-up remaining costs and a separate recursion stack. It is not LIMMARK, REC_A, MA*, A* with an OPEN list, learned IDA*IM, or a generic A*/IDA* hybrid title; the zero-additional-graph-memory endpoint does not make the complete method an IDA* alias. Preserve the inclusive UPDATE recursion test versus the adjacent strict prose comparison; MREC’s early goal-found return bypasses the final node-bound backup assignments. The actual cohort 358 collection at dd7a5a99eb412b5b587efb1e598cbb760a9bba0d contains 1,236 records (794 native and 442 pinned AIO), 4,903 identity-field occurrences including local IDs and 3,745 normalized values. Candidate IDs, names, aliases and retained source spellings have no normalized collision in that inventory. The collection includes ignored and hidden files in four-root text searches; semantic raw-search assessment is separately attributed. All 1,230 records in the older scientific-research inventory retain their bytes; six later additions were read as current definition/identity context. The seven normalized matches concern existing A*, IDA*, IDA*IM, beam-stack and RBFS-family contexts, not candidate identities. Current memory-search source owner 911 is only partially resolved; MA*/MAO* and separate IE owner 912 remain pending.",
      "claims": [
        {
          "claim_id": "stored-and-virtual-search",
          "kind": "mechanism",
          "statement": "EXPLORE descends recursively from the start. At an explicit tip it adds successors and edges when memory permits; otherwise UPDATE explores successors without adding them to the explicit graph. The algorithm uses no OPEN list.",
          "evidence": [
            {
              "source_id": "mrec1989",
              "locator": "Section 2, printed pp. 297–298 / PDF pp. 1–2; EXPLORE and UPDATE",
              "relation": "supports"
            }
          ]
        },
        {
          "claim_id": "retained-graph-estimates",
          "kind": "mechanism",
          "statement": "EXPAND initializes a newly stored successor estimate with its heuristic value and records an edge to that successor; when the successor is already in the explicit graph, it adds the edge without creating another stored node. UPDATE uses the stored estimate when available and the heuristic estimate otherwise.",
          "evidence": [
            {
              "source_id": "mrec1989",
              "locator": "Section 2, printed p. 298 / PDF p. 2; EXPAND and UPDATE pseudocode",
              "relation": "supports"
            }
          ]
        },
        {
          "claim_id": "inclusive-recursion-and-backup",
          "kind": "mechanism",
          "statement": "In the printed UPDATE pseudocode, a successor is explored recursively when its current estimate plus transition cost is less than or equal to the current node bound. The recursive bound is the current bound minus that cost. If no goal terminates the traversal early, the returned node bound is the minimum resulting successor estimate plus transition cost, and a stored node receives that updated bound; the goal-found branch instead records the path and returns before those final backup assignments.",
          "evidence": [
            {
              "source_id": "mrec1989",
              "locator": "Section 2, printed p. 298 / PDF p. 2; UPDATE pseudocode, inclusive test newb + c(n,n_i) <= bnode",
              "relation": "supports"
            }
          ]
        },
        {
          "claim_id": "extra-memory-control",
          "kind": "scope",
          "statement": "The parameter M describes storage additional to the implicit recursion stack. With no additional graph storage the method operates in the IDA* manner; with storage available it retains explicit graph information between recursive passes rather than becoming an OPEN-based A* implementation.",
          "evidence": [
            {
              "source_id": "mrec1989",
              "locator": "Abstract and Sections 1–2, printed pp. 297–299 / PDF pp. 1–3; property 1 and property 2",
              "relation": "supports"
            }
          ]
        }
      ],
      "concept_kind": "algorithm",
      "definition_evidence": [
        {
          "source_id": "mrec1989",
          "locator": "Sections 1–2, printed pp. 297–299 / PDF pp. 1–3; EXPLORE, EXPAND and UPDATE",
          "relation": "supports"
        }
      ],
      "evidence_sources": [
        {
          "source_id": "mrec1989",

        "search_scope": "Pinned AIO commit 397851c547d1c4d8f06ef184f63c1d40bc86937a, SHA-256 8f741d71408c93f15c62607106aa46f6edbc4e070c5546ed3ae111ada6e65cf6: complete 442-CLASS identity/synonym inventory mechanically searched; 104 search, planning, heuristic, graph, reasoning, memory, decision, function and learning-related definition projections read; the 12 examined CLASS nodes below read in full with scoped synonyms and all incident edges. This is a mapping assessment of this snapshot, not a global ontology-absence claim.",
        "rationale": "The inspected candidate is a source-defined heuristic search algorithm. No inspected AIO class supplies a defensible broader, narrower or specifically related mapping; the tempting graph, recursion, reasoning, task and memory classes have different defining scopes. No mapping is inferred solely from an implementation using mathematical functions or from an algorithm being used in AI.",
        "examined_targets": [
          {
            "target": "AIO:GraphLanguageModel",
            "rejection_reason": "The pinned class is a language model over graph-structured input or output. A heuristic search procedure over states and transitions is not that language-model class; graph vocabulary alone does not support a related mapping."
          },
          {
            "target": "AIO:ReasoningLLM",
            "rejection_reason": "The pinned class is an LLM for explicit logical reasoning in language tasks. A state-space search algorithm does not become an LLM because it supports reasoning."
          },
          {
            "target": "AIO:NeuroSymbolicLLM",
            "rejection_reason": "The pinned class combines neural and symbolic reasoning in an LLM. The source algorithm specifies search control without an LLM or a learned neural-symbolic architecture."
          },
          {
            "target": "AIO:RecursiveLanguageModel",
            "rejection_reason": "The pinned class is a recursive neural language model with neural composition and layer relations. Recursion in a search routine is not neural recursive composition."
          },
          {
            "target": "AIO:MachineLearningTask",
            "rejection_reason": "The pinned definition concerns processes that build methods learning from data. The source algorithm searches using supplied states, costs and heuristics; an AI algorithm is not automatically a machine-learning task."
          },

      "field": "identity_notes",
      "historical": "This record denotes MREC in Sen and Bagchi (1989), not the general best-first-search family, A*, ordinary IDA*, or the separate LIMMARK and REC_A procedures. The zero-additional-memory relationship to IDA* is an endpoint of this method, not an alias for the full configurable algorithm. The displayed UPDATE pseudocode, including its inclusive recursion test, defines the operational claim below; the adjacent prose has a different strict comparison.",
      "current": "MREC denotes Sen and Bagchi's 1989 recursive best-first memory-controlled procedure, with an explicitly stored graph and virtual unstored successors, backed-up remaining costs and a separate recursion stack. Preserve the inclusive UPDATE recursion test versus the adjacent strict prose comparison; MREC’s early goal-found return bypasses the final node-bound backup assignments.       "current": "SMA* denotes Russell's 1992 simplified memory-bounded A* tree procedure, with a node budget, incremental successor generation, pathmax, guarded completed-node backup and least-promising-node deletion with retained parent bounds.       "field": "identity_notes",
      "historical": "This record denotes Ghosh, Mahanti and Nau’s 1994 Iterative Threshold Search, called ITS in its defining paper. A bare ITS alias is omitted because it is ambiguous outside this source. The stored per-branch bounds and retraction procedure distinguish the method from ordinary IDA*, MREC, IDA* threshold-prediction models and generic beam search. The paper’s description of ITS as a generalization or simplification of earlier methods is not an equivalence assertion.",
      "current": "Iterative threshold search denotes the limited-memory tree procedure of Ghosh, Mahanti and Nau (1994), which combines cost-threshold passes with per-branch bounds including ungenerated successors, retraction and retained lower-bound information. It is distinct from ordinary smallest-excess IDA*, learned threshold-prediction IDA*IM, MREC, RBFS and beam search. The ambiguous bare acronym ITS is not added as an alias. The literal Background h(n)>0 versus Example 1 h(n)=0 discrepancy is retained. The two-tip retraction guard preserves the current path, so S=0 does not imply zero total storage.
